name: Datacenter hall
pitch: 2 MW of servers for your clients. Needs power to run.
whyItMatters: More capacity serves more clients, and every MW of servers needs more MW of power behind it.

name: Gas power plant
pitch: 6 MW, steady, cheap to build. Burns gas.
whyItMatters: Gas is reliable and compact, but every MWh emits around half a tonne of CO2 over its life cycle.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, Table A.III.2: life-cycle median for gas combined cycle 490 gCO2e/kWh (range 410-650). https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/02/ipcc_wg3_ar5_annex-iii.pdf Build and running costs are game values.

name: Coal power plant
pitch: 10 MW, the cheapest power per MWh. Also the dirtiest.
whyItMatters: Coal packs a lot of power on little land, at the highest carbon and air-pollution cost of any source.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, Table A.III.2: life-cycle median for coal (pulverised) 820 gCO2e/kWh (range 740-910). https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/02/ipcc_wg3_ar5_annex-iii.pdf Build and running costs are game values.

name: Biomass plant
pitch: 5 MW from burning wood. Sounds green.
whyItMatters: Burning wood emits CO2 now; regrowing forests take decades to absorb it. Whether it is green depends on where the wood comes from.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, Table A.III.2: life-cycle median for dedicated biomass 230 gCO2e/kWh, range 130-420 (excludes land-use change, hence debated). https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/02/ipcc_wg3_ar5_annex-iii.pdf Build and running costs are game values.

name: Wind farm
pitch: 9 MW of turbines. Delivers about a third of that, when the wind blows.
whyItMatters: Wind is clean and cheap to run, but it needs a lot of land per MW and it does not blow on demand.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, Table A.III.2: life-cycle median for onshore wind 11 gCO2e/kWh. Capacity factor: IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2023, global weighted average for new onshore wind 36 % (IPCC full-load hours 1800-3500 h/yr = 21-40 %). https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/02/ipcc_wg3_ar5_annex-iii.pdf ; https://www.irena.org/-/media/Files/IRENA/Agency/Publication/2024/Sep/IRENA_Renewable_power_generation_costs_in_2023.pdf Build and running costs are game values.

name: Solar farm
pitch: 12 MW of panels. Delivers a sixth of that on average. Better in the south.
whyItMatters: Solar is clean and cheap to run, but only works by day: a sunny site produces twice as much as a northern one.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, Table A.III.2: life-cycle median for utility-scale PV 48 gCO2e/kWh. Capacity factor: IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2023, global weighted average for new utility PV 16 %; IPCC full-load hours 1200-2400 h/yr (a 2x spread between poor and good sites). https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/02/ipcc_wg3_ar5_annex-iii.pdf ; https://www.irena.org/-/media/Files/IRENA/Agency/Publication/2024/Sep/IRENA_Renewable_power_generation_costs_in_2023.pdf Build and running costs are game values.

name: Hydro dam
pitch: Big, clean, steady power from the river. The valley floods.
whyItMatters: Hydro is low-carbon and dependable, but a dam floods land, blocks fish and changes the river for everyone downstream.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014) Annex III, Table A.III.2: life-cycle median for hydropower 24 gCO2e/kWh (range 1-2200: reservoirs can emit methane). Capacity factor: IRENA 2023, new hydropower 53 %; game uses 45 %. https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/02/ipcc_wg3_ar5_annex-iii.pdf ; https://www.irena.org/-/media/Files/IRENA/Agency/Publication/2024/Sep/IRENA_Renewable_power_generation_costs_in_2023.pdf Build and running costs are game values.
